correctness.rationale: The exact minimum-word-generator rank is proved using the fact that any factorization of a length-two target consists either of a single length-two generator or two single-letter generators. Rank n equals induced-edge sparsity, hence the n-edge/n-vertex multigraph is a disjoint union of unicyclic components. Any nontrivial same-alphabet factorization necessarily has a nonempty proper set B of one-letter images with e(B)=|B|, and any such B explicitly gives a factorization with both factors nonautomorphisms. In a pseudoforest such a proper tight B exists exactly when its cycle does not span all vertices. Cycle orientations produce the irreducible counts, and the labeled exponential formula with rooted oriented trees proves the EGF. The finite verifier independently enumerates distinct word-image sets through n=5, direct candidate factor bases through n=4, and rational series coefficients. These tests do not substitute for the proofs.

value.rationale: Free-semigroup irreducibility is a current noncommutative algebraic classification problem; constant length two is the first nontrivial uniform substitution class. The result yields complete structural iff conditions, an explicit exact all-n irreducible count with exponential rarity, and a computable EGF for rank-preserving members. This is not an arbitrary isolated finite count or a renaming of the general factor-basis theorem.
